chunk_themes.description: This theme examines the Old Testament sacrificial system, its meaning, and its fulfillment in Christ. It argues against penal substitution and emphasizes sacrifice as a meal of reconciliation, repentance, and the role of blood in atonement.

chunk_themes.title: Latin Theology and Orthodox Response
chunk_themes.description: This theme contrasts Latin (Western) theological developments with Orthodox theology, focusing on issues like the essence-energies distinction, merit, and the nature of salvation. It critiques the influence of nominalism and penal substitution on Western Christianity.

chunk_themes.title: Christianity and Paganism: Continuities and Contrasts
chunk_themes.description: This theme explores the relationship between Christianity and pagan religions, including the use of pagan concepts and the rejection of pagan practices. It covers topics like the Christmas date, the virgin birth, and the uniqueness of Christian revelation.

chunk_themes.title: Salvation and Theosis
chunk_themes.description: This theme covers the biblical meaning of salvation, emphasizing that it is not merely forensic justification but a transformative process of becoming like God (theosis). It includes the role of the Incarnation, the Harrowing of Hades, and the trans-temporal nature of resurrection.

chunk_themes.title: Passion Narratives in the Gospels
chunk_themes.description: This theme focuses on the Passion narratives in all four Gospels, emphasizing the importance of reading each account separately to understand their unique theological perspectives. It discusses the events of Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection, and their significance for salvation.

chunk_themes.title: Blood, Martyrdom, and Atonement
chunk_themes.description: This theme explores the biblical theology of blood, martyrdom, and atonement. It discusses the significance of blood in sacrifice and covenant, the role of martyrdom in witnessing to Christ, and how these concepts relate to the atonement.

chunk_themes.title: Apocryphal Acts and Apostolic Tradition
chunk_themes.description: Explores the non-canonical Acts of the Apostles, their historical reliability, and their role as witnesses to pre-existing apostolic traditions. Discusses the relationship between oral tradition and written texts, and the criteria for canonicity.

chunk_themes.title: Samaritan History and Theology
chunk_themes.description: Covers the origins, identity, and religious significance of the Samaritans, including their relationship with the northern kingdom of Israel, their sacred mountain Gerizim, and their role in the New Testament as a bridge to the Gentiles.

chunk_themes.title: The Shepherd of Hermas and Early Christian Authority
chunk_themes.description: Examines the Shepherd of Hermas, its authorship, dating, and theological content, including its treatment of post-baptismal sin and the church as a tower. Discusses its authoritative status in early Christianity and its relation to the canon.

chunk_themes.title: Gnosticism and the Orthodox Response
chunk_themes.description: Addresses the threat of Gnosticism in early Christianity and the Orthodox response, including the use of apocryphal texts to counter it. Discusses the identification of Gnostic elements in certain texts and the Church's rejection of dualistic teachings.

chunk_themes.title: Conversion and Catechesis in the Modern Church
chunk_themes.description: Focuses on the recent surge of converts to Orthodox Christianity, the challenges of catechesis, and the need for practical formation in parish life. Discusses the role of clergy and laity in welcoming and integrating newcomers.

chunk_themes.title: Modern Society and the Orthodox Community
chunk_themes.description: Analyzes contemporary social issues such as alienation, shame, and the collapse of purpose, and how the Orthodox Church offers a new start and genuine community. Draws on sociological and philosophical insights to address the challenges of modern life.

chunk_themes.title: Eschatology and Judgment
chunk_themes.description: Explores themes of death, judgment, and the afterlife, including the imagery of the hellmouth and the biblical basis for hell as a warning to believers. Discusses the restoration of all things and the hope of resurrection.

chunk_themes.title: Scripture and Holy Tradition
chunk_themes.description: Discusses the relationship between Scripture and Holy Tradition in Orthodox theology, emphasizing that Scripture is part of Tradition and that the Church's use of texts determines their authority. Addresses the Protestant doctrine of Sola Scriptura.

chunk_themes.title: Continuationism and Prophetic Gifts
chunk_themes.description: Addresses the Orthodox belief that visions and prophetic gifts continue after the apostolic era, contrary to cessationism. Uses examples from the New Testament and early Christian texts to support this view.

chunk_themes.title: Orthodox Practice and Liturgical Life
chunk_themes.description: Covers practical aspects of Orthodox Christian life, including the liturgical services, the sacraments, and the importance of forming habits of worship and prayer. Discusses the role of the laity and the need for practical catechesis.

chunk_themes.title: Online Community and Discernment
chunk_themes.description: Examines the challenges of online Orthodox content and the need for discernment based on the fruits of the Spirit. Warns against new converts creating content and emphasizes the importance of real community over parasocial relationships.

chunk_themes.title: Pastoral Care and Community Integration
chunk_themes.description: Discusses the practical challenges of pastoral care in the context of a clergy shortage and a surge of converts. Emphasizes the role of lay ministry and the need for integrating newcomers into the parish community.

chunk_themes.title: Christology and Atonement
chunk_themes.description: Explores Orthodox Christology, including the rejection of adoptionism and the understanding of Christ's death as a victory over death and the curse. Discusses theosis and the restoration of the Tree of Life.

global_themes.title: Angelology and Spiritual Warfare
global_themes.description: This theme covers the nature, hierarchy, and roles of angels and demons, including the divine council, the fall of angels, and the ongoing spiritual battle between God and evil forces. It also explores the identification of pagan gods with fallen angels and the practical means of resisting demonic influence.

global_themes.title: Christology and Incarnation
global_themes.description: This theme focuses on the person and work of Jesus Christ, including His pre-incarnate appearances in the Old Testament, His incarnation, crucifixion, resurrection, and ascension. It explores His role as the Messiah, the fulfillment of Old Testament types, and His victory over death and the devil.

global_themes.title: Atonement and Sacrifice
global_themes.description: This theme explores the biblical understanding of sacrifice, atonement, and purification, including the Day of Atonement, the Eucharist, and the crucifixion of Christ. It contrasts penal substitution with participatory and cosmic atonement, emphasizing the victory over sin and death.

global_themes.title: Theosis and Deification
global_themes.description: This theme covers the Orthodox understanding of salvation as becoming partakers of the divine nature, becoming like God, and joining the heavenly hosts. It emphasizes the transformative process of theosis, the role of the Incarnation, and the ultimate destiny of humanity.

global_themes.title: Divine Council and Angelic Hierarchy
global_themes.description: This theme explores the heavenly assembly of spiritual beings over which God presides, including the ranks and roles of angels, and the biblical concept of 'gods' as members of this council. It also covers the fall of some angels and the ongoing spiritual warfare.

global_themes.title: Spiritual Warfare and Demonic Forces
global_themes.description: This theme addresses the reality of demonic powers, their influence on individuals and societies, and the Christian response through spiritual warfare. It includes demonic possession, the 'world' as a demonic social order, and the power of baptism and the Eucharist in overcoming evil.

global_themes.title: Sacraments and Liturgy
global_themes.description: This theme covers the sacramental life of the Church, including baptism, chrismation, Eucharist, confession, ordination, and marriage. It explores their biblical roots, theological meaning, and practical implications for the life of the Church, as well as the liturgical context in which they are celebrated.

global_themes.title: Scripture and Hermeneutics
global_themes.description: This theme explores how Scripture is interpreted within the Orthodox tradition, emphasizing the role of the Church Fathers, the Holy Spirit, and the principle of trust in bishops. It addresses the dangers of liberal theology and the importance of reading Scripture in the context of the Church.

global_themes.title: Creation and the Cosmos
global_themes.description: This theme covers the biblical view of creation, including the spiritual realities of the sea, the deep, and the heavenly bodies, and the re-enchantment of science. It explores the relationship between God, humanity, and the cosmos, and the human vocation to continue the work of ordering creation.

global_themes.title: Eschatology and the Afterlife
global_themes.description: This theme covers the final things: the Second Coming, the resurrection of the dead, the Last Judgment, and the eternal state. It explores the biblical imagery of the Day of the Lord, the Millennium, the Antichrist, and the final defeat of evil, emphasizing the present reality of the Messianic Age and the hope of bodily resurrection.

global_themes.title: Theology of God and Trinity
global_themes.description: This theme explores the nature of God, the Trinity, and the relationship between the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. It includes discussions of the two powers in heaven, the hypostases, and the incarnation, as well as the distinction between God's essence and energies.

global_themes.title: Anthropology and Human Person
global_themes.description: This theme explores the nature of the human person as body and soul, the image of God, and the effects of the Fall on human nature. It critiques Platonic dualism and emphasizes the soul as the life of the body, with eternal life defined as knowing God.

global_themes.title: Paganism and Idolatry
global_themes.description: This theme examines the biblical polemic against pagan deities and practices, showing how Scripture subverts and reinterprets ancient Near Eastern mythology. It includes the Baal Cycle, divine smack talk, and the inversion of pagan rituals, as well as the Christian response to pagan religion.

global_themes.title: Saints and the Theotokos
global_themes.description: This theme covers the veneration of saints and relics, the concept of theosis, and the belief that saints become places where God dwells. It includes the theological foundations for relics and the intercession of the saints, with special focus on the Virgin Mary as the Theotokos and Queen Mother.

global_themes.title: Old Testament Foundations
global_themes.description: This theme covers the historical and theological foundations of the Old Testament, including the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings, and how they are interpreted in light of Christ and the New Testament. It includes discussions of the Exodus, the Law, the temple, and the priesthood.

global_themes.title: Church and Ecclesiology
global_themes.description: This theme explores the nature of the Church as the body of Christ, the priesthood of all believers, and the importance of community and tradition. It covers the Church's structure, the role of bishops and priests, and the relationship between doctrine and practice.

global_themes.title: Spiritual Life and Practice
global_themes.description: This theme covers the practices and disciplines of the Christian life, including prayer, fasting, almsgiving, and the pursuit of theosis. It emphasizes the importance of asceticism, the struggle against passions, and the goal of union with God.

global_themes.title: Prophecy and Apocalyptic
global_themes.description: This theme explores the genre of apocalypse as revelation, the prophetic tradition, and the Day of the Lord. It includes the role of prophets like Elijah and John the Forerunner, and the unveiling of spiritual realities behind historical events.

global_themes.title: Time and Eternity
global_themes.description: This theme explores the nature of time from an Orthodox perspective, arguing that God is not bound by time and that time is a phenomenological experience of creatures. It critiques views like Calvinism and open theism that presuppose God's temporality, and discusses the liturgical calendar as a means of theosis.

global_themes.title: Election and Predestination
global_themes.description: This theme discusses the biblical concept of election (being chosen) in light of Orthodox theology, rejecting Calvinist double predestination and open theism. It emphasizes that God's foreknowledge is not deterministic and that election is corporate and Christ-centered.

global_themes.title: Modernity and Culture
global_themes.description: This theme critiques modern and postmodern concepts of religion, individualism, and progress, contrasting them with the Orthodox understanding of religion as a way of being in the world. It examines the Axial Age and the Neolithic Revolution as historical shifts that shaped religious practice and belief.

global_themes.title: Second Temple Judaism
global_themes.description: This theme situates Christianity within the context of Second Temple Judaism, emphasizing its continuity with Jewish apocalyptic and wisdom traditions. It discusses the diversity of Jewish beliefs about angels, demons, and the afterlife, and how early Christianity emerged as a Jewish movement.

global_themes.title: Ethics and Moral Theology
global_themes.description: This theme engages with philosophical and theological questions about the nature of good and evil, the basis of morality, and the role of divine commands. It critiques modern ethical theories and presents an Orthodox Christian alternative centered on participation in God's energies.

global_themes.title: History and Tradition
global_themes.description: This theme explores the Orthodox understanding of history as sacred narrative and the role of tradition in preserving the faith. It covers the history of the Church, the ecumenical councils, and the development of doctrine.

global_themes.title: The Fall and Original Sin
global_themes.description: This theme explores the biblical account of the fall of humanity and angels, the origin of death and mortality, and the consequences for the world. It covers the roles of Adam, Cain, and the Tower of Babel, and the impact of sin on the cosmos.
